**Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

Roopa said to me, "Please accompany me to the market."

options.text: Roopa said please accompany me to the market.
Roopa said to me that you must accompany me to the market.
Roopa is requesting me to accompany her to the market.
Roopa requested me to accompany her to the market.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Roopa requested me to accompany her to the market.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given direct speech is an imperative sentence. An imperative sentence is a sentence that expresses a command, a request, advice, or a suggestion.
 
 
• *Open the door. **(Command)***
 
• *Please help me.** (Request)***
 
• *Quit smoking.** (Advice.)***
 
 
 
• As imperative sentences have a command, a request, advice, or a suggestion, to change them into an indirect speech some specific verbs are used (requested, order, advised, forbade, suggested) to replace the verbs (e.g. told, said) of reporting verb.
 
• In the given sentence, 'please' is used which gives the tone of requesting somebody. Hence, use *'requested' in the reported speech.*

**So the correct Indirect speech is**→* Roopa **requested **me to accompany her to the market.*

Choose the option that is the correct indirect form of the sentence.

She said, "I will be available tomorrow."

options.text: She said that she would be available tomorrow.
She said that she would be available the next day.
She said that she must be available the next day.
She said that she will be available the next day.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'She said that she would be available the next day'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **correct indirect form** of the sentence *"She said, 'I will be available tomorrow.'*" is *"She said that she would be available the next day."*
 
• **When changing direct speech into indirect speech, t**he verb tense typically shifts back (this is known as "backshifting").
 
• In this case, **"will" **becomes "**would".**
 
• Moreover, words indicating nearness in time or place in direct speech are generally changed into words showing distance in indirect speech.
 
• Here, **"tomorrow" **changes to** "the next day".**

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: '*She said that she would be available the next day.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1, "She said that she would be available tomorrow,"** is incorrect because "tomorrow" should be changed to "the next day" in indirect speech.
 
• **Option 3, "She said that she must be available the next day,**" is incorrect because "will" should not change to "must" in indirect speech. "Must" changes the meaning, implying a necessity or obligation that wasn't present in the original sentence.
 
• **Option 4, "She said that she will be available the next day,"** is incorrect because the verb "will" should be backshifted to "would" in indirect speech.
